title.raw: 卷一百四十七 志9: 刑法志 Volume 147: Treatises 9 Punishment and Law

sentences.zh: 刑法志

translations.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on Punishment and Law

sentences.zh: （案：《刑法志序》，《永樂大典》原闕。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The preface to the Treatise on Punishment and Law is missing in the original Yongle Dadian.)⟩
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: The preface to the Treatise on Punishment and Law is absent from the Yongle Dadian source.)⟩

sentences.zh: 梁太祖開平三年十一月，詔太常卿李燕、御史蕭頃、中書舍人張兗、戶部侍郎崔沂、大理卿王鄯、刑部郎中崔誥，共刪定律令格式。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping, Emperor Taizu of Liang ordered the Director of Court Ceremonies Li Yan, Imperial Censor Xiao Xiang, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Director of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Shan, and Bureau Director of Punishments Cui Hao jointly to revise and fix the statutes, orders, formats, and precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping, Liang Taizu ordered Li Yan, Xiao Xiang, Zhang Chong, Cui Yi, Wang Shan, and Cui Hao to revise the statutes, orders, formats, and administrative rules together.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，宰臣薛貽矩奏：「太常卿李燕等重刊定律令三十卷，式二十卷，格一十卷，並目錄一十三卷，律疏三十卷，凡五部一十帙，共一百三卷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Chief Minister Xue Yiju memorialized: "The Director of Court Ceremonies Li Yan and others have newly printed and fixed the statutes in thirty juan, the formats in twenty juan, the precedents in ten juan, together with a table of contents in thirteen juan and the commentary on the statutes in thirty juan—in all five sections, ten cases, totaling one hundred and three juan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Chief Minister Xue Yiju reported that Li Yan and his colleagues had reprinted the statutes in thirty fascicles, formats in twenty, precedents in ten, plus thirteen fascicles of catalogue and thirty of statutory commentary—five sets in ten cases, 103 fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 敕中書舍人李仁儉詣閣門奉進，伏請目為《大梁新定格式律令》，仍頒下施行。

translations.literal: An order was issued for Secretariat Drafter Li Renjian to proceed to the Gate of Audience and present them respectfully, humbly requesting that they be titled Newly Fixed Formats, Statutes, and Orders of the Great Liang and promulgated for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renjian, a Secretariat drafter, was sent to present the work at the palace gate with a request to entitle it the Newly Fixed Formats, Statutes, and Orders of the Great Liang and to put it into effect throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: （原註：是時，大理卿李保殷進所撰《刑律總要》十二卷。）〉

translations.literal: (Original note: At this time the Director of the Court of Judicial Review Li Baoyin presented the General Essentials of Criminal Statutes in twelve juan, which he had compiled.)⟩
translations.idiomatic: (At the same time, Judicial Review Director Li Baoyin submitted his twelve-fascicle General Essentials of Criminal Statutes.)⟩

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光元年十二月，御史臺奏：「當司刑部、大理寺本朝法書，自朱溫僭逆，刪改事條，或重貨財，輕入人命，或自徇枉過，濫加刑罰。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, the Censorate memorialized: "The legal books of our dynasty held by the Ministry of Punishments and the Court of Judicial Review—since Zhu Wen's usurpation and rebellion—have had their articles deleted and altered, sometimes valuing property heavily and human life lightly, sometimes indulging personal wrongdoing and adding punishments indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tongguang 1, the Censorate reported that the Tang legal codes in the Ministry of Punishments and Court of Judicial Review had been tampered with under Zhu Wen's rebel regime—sometimes treating money as more important than life, sometimes piling on penalties to cover officials' own misconduct.

sentences.zh: 今見在三司收貯刑書，並是偽廷刪改者，兼偽廷先下諸道追取本朝法書焚毀，或經兵火所遺，皆無舊本節目。

translations.literal: The criminal law books now in the custody of the three offices are all versions revised by the usurper court; moreover the usurper court had earlier ordered the circuits to seize and burn our dynasty's legal books, and those that survived war and fire lack the old table of contents.
translations.idiomatic: Every penal code now held by the three ministries is a Liang-era revision, and the rebel court had already ordered the circuits to hunt down and burn Tang law books; what survived fire and war no longer matched the original tables of contents.

sentences.zh: 只定州敕庫有本朝法書具在，請敕定州節度使速寫副本進納，庶刑法令式，並合本朝舊制。

translations.literal: Only the edict repository at Ding Prefecture still has our dynasty's legal books intact; we request an order to the military governor of Ding Prefecture to copy them quickly and submit the copies, so that criminal statutes, orders, and formats may all accord with our dynasty's former system.
translations.idiomatic: Only the edict archive at Dingzhou still held complete Tang codes; they asked that the Dingzhou governor be ordered to copy and forward them at once so penal statutes, orders, and formats could be restored to the Tang system.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 未幾，定州王都進納唐朝格式律令，凡二百八十六卷。

translations.literal: Before long, Wang Du of Ding Prefecture presented the Tang formats, statutes, and orders—in all two hundred and eighty-six juan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Du of Dingzhou forwarded the Tang formats, statutes, and orders—286 fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，刑部尚書盧價奏，纂集《同光刑律統類》凡一十三卷，上之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Minister of Punishments Lu Jia memorialized that he had compiled the Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Criminal Statutes in thirteen juan and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2, Minister of Punishments Lu Jia submitted the thirteen-fascicle Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Criminal Statutes that he had compiled.

sentences.zh: 周太祖廣順元年六月，敕侍御史盧億、刑部員外郎曹匪躬、大理正段濤同議定重寫法書一百四十八卷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Guangshun of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, an edict ordered Attending Censor Lu Yi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Punishments Cao Feigong, and Senior Rectifier of the Court of Judicial Review Duan Tao jointly to deliberate and fix a rewritten legal corpus of one hundred and forty-eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangshun 1, Zhou Taizu ordered Attending Censor Lu Yi, Vice Director Cao Feigong of the Ministry of Punishments, and Senior Rectifier Duan Tao of the Court of Judicial Review to redraft the law books in 148 fascicles.

sentences.zh: 先是，漢隱帝末，因兵亂法書亡失，至是大理奏重寫律令格式、統類編敕，凡改點畫及義理之誤字凡二百一十有四，以晉、漢及國初事關刑法敕條，凡二十六件，分為二卷，附於編敕，目為《大周續編敕》，命省、寺行用焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Emperor Yindi of Han, the legal books were lost in the turmoil of war; thereupon the Court of Judicial Review memorialized to rewrite the statutes, orders, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts, correcting in all two hundred and fourteen erroneous characters in strokes or meaning; twenty-six items concerning criminal law from the Jin, Han, and the opening of the state were divided into two juan, appended to the compiled edicts, titled Continued Compiled Edicts of the Great Zhou, and ordered for use by the ministries and courts.
translations.idiomatic: After the law books were lost in the wars at the end of Later Han, the Court of Judicial Review proposed rewriting statutes, orders, formats, compendia, and compiled edicts, correcting 214 mistaken characters in form or meaning, and appending twenty-six criminal edicts from Jin, Han, and early Zhou in two fascicles entitled the Great Zhou Continued Compiled Edicts for use by the ministries and courts.

sentences.zh: （《宋史》：盧億，周初為侍御史，漢末兵亂，法書亡失，至是大理奏重寫律令格式、統類編敕，乃詔億與刑部員外曹匪躬、大理正段濤同加議定舊本，以京兆府改同五府，開封、大名府改同河南府，長安、萬年改為次赤縣，開封、浚儀、大名、元城改為赤縣，又定東京諸門薰風等為京城門，明德等為皇城門，啟運等為宮城門，升龍等為宮門，崇元等為殿門，廟諱書不成字，凡改點畫及義理之誤字二百一十有四。

translations.literal: (Song History: Lu Yi, in early Zhou served as Attending Censor; at the end of Han the legal books were lost in military disorder; thereupon the Court of Judicial Review memorialized to rewrite statutes, orders, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts, and an edict ordered Yi together with Vice Director of Punishments Cao Feigong and Senior Rectifier Duan Tao jointly to deliberate on the old text: Jingzhao Prefecture was changed to rank with the Five Prefectures; Kaifeng and Daming prefectures were changed to rank with Henan Prefecture; Chang'an and Wannian were made secondary red counties; Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng were made red counties; furthermore the gates of the Eastern Capital such as Xunfeng were designated capital-city gates, Mingde and others imperial-city gates, Qiyun and others palace-city gates, Shenglong and others palace gates, Chongyuan and others hall gates; taboo characters for temple names were written incompletely; in all two hundred and fourteen erroneous characters in strokes or meaning were corrected.
translations.idiomatic: (According to the Song History, Lu Yi was an attending censor in early Zhou. After the law books were lost in the Later Han wars, the Court of Judicial Review sought a rewrite, and Yi was ordered with Cao Feigong and Duan Tao to revise the old text: Jingzhao was raised to rank with the Five Prefectures; Kaifeng and Daming were equated with Henan; Chang'an and Wannian became secondary "red" counties while Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng became primary red counties; Eastern Capital gates were classified as capital, imperial-city, palace-city, palace, and hall gates; temple taboos were written with incomplete characters; and 214 erroneous characters were corrected.)

sentences.zh: 又以晉、漢及周初事關刑法敕條者，分為二卷，附編敕，目為《大周續編敕》。

translations.literal: Furthermore edict articles concerning criminal law from Jin, Han, and early Zhou were divided into two juan, appended to the compiled edicts, and titled Continued Compiled Edicts of the Great Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal edicts from Jin, Han, and early Zhou were collected in two fascicles appended to the compiled edicts under the title Great Zhou Continued Compiled Edicts.

sentences.zh: 詔行之。）〉

translations.literal: An edict ordered them put into effect.)⟩
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered their promulgation.)⟩

sentences.zh: 二年二月，中書門下奏：「準元年正月五日赦書節文，今後應犯竊盜贓及和奸者，並依晉天福元年已前條制施行。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, the Secretariat memorialized: "According to the section of the amnesty of the fifth day of the first month of the first year, hereafter those who commit theft of stolen goods and consensual adultery shall all be punished according to the regulations in force before the first year of Tianfu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2, the Secretariat reported that under the amnesty clause of the fifth day of the first month of year 1, future cases of theft and consensual adultery should be judged by the rules in force before Jin Tianfu 1.

sentences.zh: 諸處犯罪人等，除反逆罪外，其餘罪並不籍沒家產、誅及骨肉，一依格令處分者。

translations.literal: Criminals everywhere, except for crimes of rebellion and treason, for all other crimes shall not have their household property confiscated nor their kin executed, but shall be dealt with entirely according to statutes and precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Except for treason, offenders were not to have their property confiscated or their families executed, but were to be punished only as statutes and precedents prescribed.

sentences.zh: 請再下明敕，頒示天下。

translations.literal: We request that a clear edict be issued again and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that a clear edict be reissued and proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔曰：「赦書節文，明有厘革，切慮邊城遠郡，未得審詳，宜更申明，免至差誤。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an imperial pronouncement was issued: "The section of the amnesty clearly institutes reforms; we are deeply concerned that frontier cities and distant prefectures may not have understood them in detail; they should be clarified again to avoid error.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then proclaimed that the amnesty reforms might not have reached remote border districts in full and should be restated clearly to prevent mistakes.

sentences.zh: 其盜賊，若是強盜，並準自來格條斷遣；

translations.literal: As for robbers, if they are armed robbers, they shall all be sentenced and dispatched according to the established precedent articles;
translations.idiomatic: Armed robbers were to be sentenced under the long-standing precedent articles;

sentences.zh: 其犯竊盜者，計贓絹滿三匹已上者，並集眾決殺，其絹以本處上估價為定，不滿三匹者，等第決斷。

translations.literal: those who commit theft shall, when the stolen goods in silk amount to three bolts or more, all be executed by public assembly; the silk shall be valued at the highest local estimate; if less than three bolts, sentence shall be determined by gradation.
translations.idiomatic: petty thieves whose loot in silk reached three bolts or more were to be executed in public assembly, valuing silk at the highest local price; below three bolts, penalties were to be graded accordingly.

sentences.zh: 應有夫婦人被強奸者，男子決殺，婦人不坐；

translations.literal: where a married woman has been forcibly violated, the man shall be executed by assembly and the woman shall not be punished;
translations.idiomatic: In cases of rape of a married woman, the man was to be executed and the woman was not to be punished;

sentences.zh: 其犯和奸者，並準律科斷，罪不至死。

translations.literal: those who commit consensual adultery shall all be sentenced according to the statutes, the crime not reaching death.
translations.idiomatic: consensual adultery was to be punished under the statutes, short of the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 其餘奸私罪犯，準格律處分。

translations.literal: All other illicit sexual offenses shall be dealt with according to statutes and precedents.
translations.idiomatic: All other sexual offenses were to be handled under statutes and precedents.

sentences.zh: 應諸色罪人，除謀反大逆外，其餘並不得誅殺骨肉、籍沒家產。

translations.literal: All criminals of every kind, except for plotting rebellion and great treason, for the rest must not have their kin executed nor their household property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Except for plotting rebellion or great treason, no offender's kin were to be executed and no household property was to be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 」先是，晉天福中敕，凡和奸者，男子婦人並處極法，至是始改從律文焉。

translations.literal: " Earlier, in an edict of the Tianfu era of Jin, all who committed consensual adultery, man and woman alike, were punished by the extreme penalty; only at this time was it first changed to follow the statutory text.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a Jin Tianfu edict had imposed the death penalty on both parties in consensual adultery; only now was the statute restored.

sentences.zh: 世宗顯德四年五月，中書門下奏：「準宣，法書行用多時，文意古質，條目繁細，使人難會，兼前後敕格，互換重疊，亦難詳定。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Xiande of Emperor Shizong, the Secretariat memorialized: "According to the imperial instruction, the legal books have been in use for a long time; their language is archaic, their articles numerous and minute, making them hard to understand; moreover edicts and precedents before and after overlap and repeat, and are also hard to fix definitively.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xiande 4, Shizong's Secretariat reported that the law books had long been in force but their archaic, minute wording was hard to follow, and successive edicts and precedents overlapped in ways that were hard to reconcile.

sentences.zh: 宜令中書門下並重刪定，務從節要，所貴天下易為詳究者。

translations.literal: The Secretariat should be ordered jointly to revise and fix them again, striving for brevity and essentials, so that throughout the realm they may easily be studied in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat should be ordered to revise them again for brevity so that the whole realm could study them with ease.

sentences.zh: 伏以刑法者御人之銜勒，救弊之斧斤，故鞭撲不可一日弛之於家，刑法不可一日廢之於國，雖堯、舜淳古之代，亦不能舍此而致理矣。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that criminal law is the bridle by which people are governed and the axe by which abuses are remedied; therefore flogging cannot for one day be relaxed in the family, nor criminal law for one day abolished in the state—even in the pure antiquity of Yao and Shun one could not discard this and achieve good order.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal law, they argued, was the bridle of governance and the axe against abuse: flogging could not be suspended for a day in the household, nor penal law in the state—even Yao and Shun could not govern well without it.

sentences.zh: 今奉制旨刪定律令，有以見聖君欽恤明罰敕法之意也。

translations.literal: Now, receiving the imperial order to revise the statutes and orders, one may see the sage ruler's intent to revere compassion, clarify punishments, and instruct in law.
translations.idiomatic: Obeying the order to revise statutes and orders showed the sage ruler's care to clarify punishments and teach the law.

sentences.zh: 竊以律令之書，政理之本，經聖賢之損益，為古今之章程，歷代以來，謂之彜典。

translations.literal: We venture that books of statutes and orders are the foundation of government; revised through gain and loss by sages, they serve as regulations for past and present; through successive ages they have been called the constant canon.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and orders were the foundation of government, refined by sages through the ages into the enduring canon of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷之所行用者律一十二卷、律疏三十卷、式二十卷、令三十卷、《開成格》一十卷、《大中統類》一十二卷、後唐以來至漢末編敕三十二卷及皇朝制敕等。

translations.literal: What the court now employs are the statutes in twelve juan, the commentary on the statutes in thirty juan, the formats in twenty juan, the orders in thirty juan, the Kaicheng Precedents in ten juan, the Dazhong Comprehensive Categories in twelve juan, thirty-two juan of compiled edicts from Later Tang down to the end of Han, and the present dynasty's regulatory edicts, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: The court currently used twelve fascicles of statutes, thirty of commentary, twenty of formats, thirty of orders, ten of Kaicheng Precedents, twelve of Dazhong Comprehensive Categories, thirty-two fascicles of compiled edicts from Later Tang through Later Han, and the dynasty's own regulatory edicts.

sentences.zh: 折獄定刑，無出於此。

translations.literal: In deciding cases and fixing punishments, nothing lies outside these.
translations.idiomatic: All trials and sentences depended on these texts.

sentences.zh: 律令則文辭古質，看覽者難以詳明；

translations.literal: The statutes and orders have archaic language, and readers find them hard to understand clearly;
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and orders were written in archaic language that readers found hard to grasp;

sentences.zh: 格敕則條目繁多，檢閱者或有疑誤。

translations.literal: the precedents and edicts have numerous articles, and those who consult them may harbor doubts and errors.
translations.idiomatic: precedents and edicts had so many articles that officials consulting them often went astray.

sentences.zh: 加之邊遠之地，貪猾之徒，緣此為奸，浸以成弊。

translations.literal: Moreover in remote regions greedy and cunning persons take advantage of this to commit wrongdoing, which gradually becomes abuse.
translations.idiomatic: In remote regions, greedy and cunning men exploited the confusion, and abuses spread.

sentences.zh: 方屬盛明之運，宜伸畫一之規，所冀民不陷刑，吏知所守。

translations.literal: Now in an age of flourishing brilliance, a uniform standard should be extended, so that the people may not fall into punishment and officials may know what to uphold.
translations.idiomatic: In this flourishing age a single clear standard was needed so that the people would not be trapped in punishment and officials would know their duty.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，望準聖旨施行，仍差侍御史知雜事張湜、太子右庶子劇可久、殿中侍御史率汀、職方郎中鄧守中、倉部郎中王瑩、司封員外郎賈比、太常博士趙礪、國子博士李光贊、大理正蘇曉、太子中允王伸等一十人，編集新格，勒成部帙。

translations.literal: Your subjects have deliberated and hope to carry out the sage instruction; we further request that Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs Zhang Chi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Kejiu, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Bureau Director of Appointments Deng Shouzhong, Bureau Director of Granaries Wang Ying, Vice Director of Seals Jia Bi, Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhao Li, Doctor of the Directorate of Education Li Guangzan, Senior Rectifier Su Xiao, and Junior Mentor Wang Shen—ten men in all—be assigned to compile a new code of precedents and bind it into a complete set.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to implement the imperial will by appointing ten officials—including Zhang Chi, Ju Kejiu, Shuai Ting, Deng Shouzhong, Wang Ying, Jia Bi, Zhao Li, Li Guangzan, Su Xiao, and Wang Shen—to compile a new code of precedents in book form.

sentences.zh: 律令之有難解者，就文訓釋；

translations.literal: Where statutes and orders are hard to understand, gloss the text in place;
translations.idiomatic: Obscure passages in statutes and orders were to be glossed in place;

sentences.zh: 格敕之有繁雜者，隨事刪除。

translations.literal: where precedents and edicts are redundant, delete according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: redundant precedents and edicts were to be cut as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 止要諧理省文，兼且直書易會。

translations.literal: One need only harmonize reason and economize text, and moreover write plainly so that it is easy to grasp.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was coherent, economical wording written plainly enough to be understood at once.

sentences.zh: 其中有輕重未當，便於古而不便於今，矛盾相違，可於此而不可於彼，盡宜改正，無或牽拘。

translations.literal: Where severity and leniency are inappropriate, where what suited antiquity does not suit the present, where provisions contradict and conflict, applicable here but not there—all should be corrected without being bound by constraint.
translations.idiomatic: Uneven penalties, rules suited to antiquity but not to the present, and contradictory provisions were all to be corrected without undue restraint.

sentences.zh: 候編集畢日，委御史臺、尚書省四品以上及兩省五品以上官參詳可否，送中書門下議定，奏取進止。

translations.literal: When compilation is complete, commission the Censorate, officials of the fourth rank and above in the Department of State Affairs, and officials of the fifth rank and above in the two secretariats to examine whether it is feasible, send it to the Secretariat for deliberation and fixing, and memorialize for imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished, the Censorate, fourth-rank officials of the Department of State Affairs, and fifth-rank officials of the two secretariats were to review it, the Secretariat was to deliberate, and a memorial was to be submitted for the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 自是湜等於都省集議刪定，仍令大官供膳。

translations.literal: Thereafter Chi and the others met at the metropolitan offices to deliberate on revision and fixing, and the Court of Imperial Entertainments was ordered to provide meals.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Zhang Chi and his colleagues met at the metropolitan offices to revise the code, with meals supplied by the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，中書門下奏：「侍御史知雜事張湜等九人，奉詔編集刑書，悉有條貫，兵部尚書張昭等一十人，參詳旨要，更加損益。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the Secretariat memorialized: "The nine men led by Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs Zhang Chi, having received the edict to compile the book of punishments, have all brought it into systematic order; Minister of War Zhang Zhao and ten others have examined the essential points and further added revisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 5, the Secretariat reported that Zhang Chi's nine-man team had compiled the penal code in good order and that Zhang Zhao's ten reviewers had refined it further.

sentences.zh: 臣質、臣溥據文評議，備見精審。

translations.literal: Your subjects Zhi and Pu have judged by the text and find it altogether precise and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Pu had reviewed the text and found it precise throughout.

sentences.zh: 其所編集者，用律為正；

translations.literal: What they have compiled takes the statutes as the standard;
translations.idiomatic: The compilation took the statutes as its foundation;

sentences.zh: 辭旨之有難解者，釋以疏意；

translations.literal: where the wording is hard to understand, it is explained by the sense of the commentary;
translations.idiomatic: obscure wording was explained from the statutory commentary;

sentences.zh: 義理之有易了者，略其疏文。

translations.literal: where the meaning is easy to grasp, the commentary text is abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: where the meaning was plain, commentary was omitted.

sentences.zh: 式令之有附近者次之，格敕之有廢置者又次之。

translations.literal: Formats and orders that are relevant come next; precedents and edicts that have been abolished come after that.
translations.idiomatic: Relevant formats and orders followed next, then superseded precedents and edicts.

sentences.zh: 事有不便於今、該說未盡者，別立新條於本條之下；

translations.literal: matters inconvenient for the present or not fully covered in explanation have new articles set up separately beneath the original article;
translations.idiomatic: Where present conditions required change or the text was incomplete, new articles were added beneath the original ones;

sentences.zh: 其有文理深古、慮人疑惑者，別以朱字訓釋。

translations.literal: where the language is profoundly archaic and readers may be puzzled, separate glosses in red characters are provided.
translations.idiomatic: deeply archaic passages that might confuse readers were glossed separately in red ink.

sentences.zh: 至於朝廷之禁令，州縣之常科，各以類分，悉令編附。

translations.literal: As for court prohibitions and the standing regulations of prefectures and counties, each is classified by category and all are ordered compiled and appended.
translations.idiomatic: Court prohibitions and the standing regulations of prefectures and counties were classified and all appended.

sentences.zh: 所冀發函展卷，綱目無遺，究本討源，刑政咸在。

translations.literal: The hope is that upon opening the case and unrolling the scroll, the outline will omit nothing, tracing root and source, so that criminal administration is all contained.
translations.idiomatic: The hope was that upon opening the volume every topic would be covered and the full scope of criminal administration would be found within.

sentences.zh: 其所編集，勒成一部，別有目錄，凡二十一卷。

translations.literal: What they have compiled is bound into one work, with a separate table of contents, in all twenty-one juan.
translations.idiomatic: The work was bound in one set with a separate catalogue, twenty-one fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 刑名之要，盡統於茲，目之為《大周刑統》，欲請頒行天下，與律疏令式通行。

translations.literal: The essentials of criminal nomenclature are all gathered here; it is titled Comprehensive Criminal Code of the Great Zhou; we wish to request promulgation throughout the realm, to be used together with the statutes, commentary, orders, and formats.
translations.idiomatic: All essentials of penal nomenclature were gathered in it under the title Comprehensive Criminal Code of the Great Zhou; they asked that it be promulgated throughout the realm alongside statutes, commentary, orders, and formats.

sentences.zh: 其《刑法統類》、《開成格》、編敕等，采掇既盡，不在法司行使之限，自來有宣命指揮公事及三司臨時條法，州縣見今施行，不在編集之數。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Categories of Criminal Law, the Kaicheng Precedents, compiled edicts, and the like have been fully drawn upon and lie outside the scope of what the judicial offices enforce; there have always been matters directed by imperial command and temporary regulations of the three offices, now in force in prefectures and counties, which are not included in the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Material from the Comprehensive Categories of Criminal Law, Kaicheng Precedents, and compiled edicts had been fully drawn upon and was no longer separately enforced by the judicial offices; standing directives and temporary regulations of the three ministries still in use locally were excluded from the compilation.

sentences.zh: 應該京百司公事，逐司各有見行條件，望令本司刪集，送中書門下詳議聞奏。

translations.literal: As for the routine business of the hundred offices of the capital, each office has its own regulations in force; we hope each office may be ordered to revise and compile them and send them to the Secretariat for detailed deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: For the routine business of the capital offices, each ministry still had its own regulations in force; they asked that each compile them and submit them to the Secretariat for review.

sentences.zh: 」敕宜依，仍頒行天下。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered compliance and further promulgation throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request and ordered promulgation throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 乃賜侍御史知雜事張湜等九人各銀器二十兩，雜彩三十匹，賞刪定《刑統》之勞也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the nine men led by Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs Zhang Chi were each granted twenty taels of silver vessels and thirty bolts of assorted silks, rewarding their labor in revising the Comprehensive Criminal Code.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chi and the other eight compilers were each rewarded with twenty taels of silver vessels and thirty bolts of assorted silks for revising the Comprehensive Criminal Code.

sentences.zh: 唐同光二年六月己巳，敕：「應御史臺河南府行臺馬步司左右軍巡院，見禁囚徒，據罪輕重，限十日內並須決遣申奏。

translations.literal: On the day jisi of the sixth month of the second year of Tongguang of Tang, an edict ordered: "All prisoners now detained by the Censorate, the Henan Prefecture Branch Secretariat, the Cavalry and Infantry Commission, and the Left and Right Army Patrol Courts, according to the severity of their crimes, must within ten days all be sentenced, dispatched, and reported in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day in the sixth month of Tongguang 2, Tang issued an edict that all prisoners held by the Censorate, the Henan Branch Secretariat, the Cavalry and Infantry Commission, and the Left and Right Army Patrol Courts were to be sentenced and reported within ten days according to the severity of their crimes.

sentences.zh: 仍委四京、諸道州府，見禁囚徒，速宜疏決，不得淹停，兼恐內外形勢官員私事寄禁，切要止絕，俾無冤滯。

translations.literal: The four capitals and the prefectures and districts of all circuits are further commissioned: prisoners now detained should promptly be cleared and sentenced, without delay; moreover, fearing that inside and outside the capital powerful officials detain people on private matters, this must be strictly stopped, so that there are no wrongful detentions.
translations.idiomatic: The four capitals and all circuit prefectures were likewise ordered to clear their dockets without delay, and to stop officials from using detention for private ends so that the innocent would not languish in jail.

sentences.zh: 」三年五月己未，敕：「在京、及諸道州府，所禁罪人，如無大過，速令疏決，不得淹滯。

translations.literal: " On the day jiwei of the fifth month of the third year, an edict ordered: "In the capital and in the prefectures and districts of all circuits, prisoners detained, if they have no grave offense, shall promptly be cleared and sentenced, without protracted delay.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day in the fifth month of year 3, another edict ordered that prisoners in the capital and in the circuits who had committed no grave offense were to be cleared promptly without prolonged detention.

sentences.zh: 」六月甲寅，敕：「刑以秋冬，雖關惻隱，罪多連累，翻慮滯淹。

translations.literal: " On the day jiayin of the sixth month, an edict ordered: "Punishment in autumn and winter, though it concerns compassion, when crimes involve many persons in joint liability, one instead fears prolonged detention.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day in the sixth month, an edict noted that although executions were traditionally held in autumn and winter out of compassion, joint-liability cases often led to prolonged detention.

sentences.zh: 若或十人之中，止為一夫抵死，豈可以輕附重，禁錮逾時。

translations.literal: If among ten persons only one man must die in requital, how can the light be attached to the heavy and imprisonment exceed its time?
translations.idiomatic: If only one man among ten must die, how could the light be bound with the heavy and kept imprisoned beyond their time?

sentences.zh: 言念哀矜，又難全廢。

translations.literal: Speaking of compassionate pity, yet it is hard to abolish it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Compassion argued against abandoning the seasonal rule altogether.

sentences.zh: 其諸司囚徒，罪無輕重，並宜各委本司，據罪詳斷申奏，輕者即時疏理，重者候過立春，至秋分然後行法。

translations.literal: Prisoners of all offices, regardless of the severity of crime, should all be entrusted to their respective offices to sentence in detail according to crime and report; the light shall be cleared promptly; the heavy shall wait until after the Beginning of Spring, and punishment shall be carried out from then until the Autumn Equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners in all offices, light or heavy, were to be sentenced by their own departments and reported: minor cases cleared at once, capital cases executed only between the Beginning of Spring and the Autumn Equinox.

sentences.zh: 如是事系軍機，須行嚴令，或謀惡逆，或畜奸邪，或行劫殺人，難於留滯，並不在此限。」

translations.literal: If the matter concerns military urgency requiring strict enforcement, or plotting wicked treason, or harboring treacherous evil, or robbery and murder, which are hard to detain—none of these are within this limit."
translations.idiomatic: Cases involving military urgency, treason, harboring traitors, or robbery and murder, which could not be delayed, were excepted from this rule."

sentences.zh: 天成元年十一月庚申，敕：「應天下州使系囚，除大辟罪以上，委所在長吏，速推勘決斷，不得傍追證對，經過食宿之地，除當死刑外，並仰釋放，兼不許懲治。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen of the eleventh month of the first year of Tiancheng, an edict ordered: "All prisoners detained by prefectural commissioners throughout the realm, except for crimes of capital punishment and above, are entrusted to the local chief officials to investigate, try, and sentence quickly; they must not be pursued on collateral evidence and confrontation; in places passed through for lodging and food, except those liable to death, all are ordered released, and punishment is also not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the eleventh month of Tiancheng 1, an edict ordered that all prisoners held by prefectural commissioners, except those facing capital punishment, were to be tried quickly by local officials without collateral pursuit of witnesses; travelers held along the route, except those liable to death, were to be released and not punished.

sentences.zh: 」二年春。

translations.literal: " In the spring of the second year.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺李同上言：「天下系囚，請委長吏逐旬親自引問，質其罪狀真虛，然後論之以法，庶無枉濫。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Li Tong memorialized: "Prisoners throughout the realm—we request that chief officials be entrusted every ten days personally to summon and question them, verify whether their crimes are true or false, and only then judge them by law, so that there may be no wrongful abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Li Tong proposed that chief officials personally question all prisoners every ten days, verify the truth of the charges, and only then apply the law, so that injustice might be avoided.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 六月，大理少卿王郁上言：「凡決極刑，合三覆奏，近年以來，全不守此。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Yu memorialized: "Whenever the extreme penalty is decided, there should be three rehearings; in recent years this has not been observed at all.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Vice Director Wang Yu of the Court of Judicial Review reported that capital sentences required three rehearings, a rule neglected in recent years.

sentences.zh: 伏乞今後前一日令各一覆奏。

translations.literal: We humbly beg that hereafter on the day before, one rehearing each be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that henceforth one rehearing be held on the day before execution.

sentences.zh: 」奉敕宜依。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered compliance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered compliance.

sentences.zh: 八月，西京奏：「奉近敕，在京犯極刑者，令決前一日各一覆奏，緣當府地遠，此後凡有極刑，不審準條疏覆奏。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Western Capital memorialized: "Having received the recent edict that those who commit the extreme penalty in the capital are to have one rehearing each on the day before execution—because our prefecture is far away, hereafter whenever there is an extreme penalty, we are uncertain whether to follow the article and report a rehearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Western Capital reported that under the recent edict capital convicts in the capital were to receive one rehearing the day before execution, but because the Western Capital was far away, they were unsure whether the rule applied to them.

sentences.zh: 」奉敕旨：「昨六月二十日所降敕文，只為應在洛京有犯極刑者覆奏，其諸道已降旨命，準舊例施行。

translations.literal: " An edict responded: "The edict issued on the twentieth day of the sixth month yesterday applied only to those who commit the extreme penalty in Luoyang; the circuits have already received imperial orders and shall follow the former precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied that the edict of the twentieth day of the sixth month applied only to capital convicts in Luoyang; the circuits were to follow the former precedent already issued to them.

sentences.zh: 今詳西京所奏，尚未明近敕，兼慮諸道有此疑惑，故令曉諭。

translations.literal: Now examining the Western Capital's memorial, the recent edict is still not clear; moreover, fearing that the circuits may have this same doubt, we therefore order clarification.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Western Capital's memorial showed the recent edict was still unclear and other circuits might share the doubt, clarification was ordered.

sentences.zh: 」十月辛丑，德音：「為政之要，切在無私；

translations.literal: " On the day xinchou of the tenth month, a benevolent pronouncement: "The essential of governing lies in being without selfishness;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day in the tenth month, a benevolent pronouncement declared that the essence of government lay in impartiality;

sentences.zh: 聽訟之方，惟期不濫。

translations.literal: the method of hearing litigation looks only to avoiding abuse.
translations.idiomatic: and the aim of hearing cases was to prevent abuse.

sentences.zh: 天下諸州府官員，如有善推疑獄及曾雪冤濫兼有異政者，當具姓名聞奏，別加甄獎。」

translations.literal: Officials of all prefectures and districts throughout the realm who are skilled in investigating doubtful cases, or who have cleared wrongful abuse and moreover have outstanding administration, shall have their names reported in memorial and receive separate selection and reward."
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the realm who skillfully resolved doubtful cases, cleared wrongful convictions, or achieved outstanding administration were to be named in memorial for special reward."

sentences.zh: 長興元年二月，制曰：「欲通和氣，必在伸冤；

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Changxing, an imperial regulation stated: "To extend harmonious qi, one must redress wrongs;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Changxing 1, an imperial regulation declared that to spread harmonious order, wrongs must be redressed;

sentences.zh: 將設公方，實資獎善。

translations.literal: to establish public rectitude truly relies on rewarding goodness.
translations.idiomatic: and to establish public justice truly required rewarding the good.

sentences.zh: 州縣官僚能雪冤獄活人生命者，許非時選，仍加階超資註官，與轉服色，已著緋者與轉兼官。

translations.literal: Prefectural and district officials who can clear wrongful cases and save human lives are permitted selection out of season, and moreover granted advancement in rank, extraordinary registration of office, change of robe color; those already wearing scarlet are granted transfer to concurrent office.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and district officials who cleared wrongful cases and saved lives might be selected out of turn, advanced in rank with extraordinary appointment, granted a change of robe color, and those already in scarlet might receive a concurrent post.

sentences.zh: 」二年二月辛亥，敕：「朕猥以眇躬，薦承鴻業，念彼疲瘵，勞於寐興。

translations.literal: " On the day xinhai of the second month of the second year, an edict ordered: "We humbly with our slight person have inherited the great enterprise, thinking of the weary and afflicted, toiling from sleep to rising.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day in the second month of year 2, an edict proclaimed that the emperor, slight in person but heir to a great enterprise, thought constantly of the weary and afflicted and toiled from sleep to waking.

sentences.zh: 或慮官不得人，因成紊亂；

translations.literal: We fear that when officials are not the right men, disorder thereby arises;
translations.idiomatic: He feared that when the wrong men held office, disorder followed;

sentences.zh: 或慮刑非其罪，遂至怨嗟。

translations.literal: or that when punishment does not match the crime, resentment and lament follow.
translations.idiomatic: or that when punishment did not fit the crime, resentment and lament followed.

sentences.zh: 王化所興，獄訟為本，茍無訓勵，必有滯淹。

translations.literal: Where royal transformation arises, litigation and imprisonment are the foundation; if there is no instruction and encouragement, there must be stagnation and delay.
translations.idiomatic: Royal transformation rested on litigation and imprisonment; without instruction and encouragement, cases would stagnate.

sentences.zh: 近日諸道百姓，或諸多違犯，或小可鬥爭。

translations.literal: Recently among the common people of the circuits, some have many violations, some petty quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: Recently among the people of the circuits, some had committed many offenses and others only petty quarrels.

sentences.zh: 官吏曲縱胥徒，巧求瑕釁。

translations.literal: Officials bend the rules to indulge clerks and runners, ingeniously seeking flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Officials indulged their clerks and runners and ingeniously hunted for pretexts.

sentences.zh: 初則滋張節目，作法拘囚；

translations.literal: At first they multiply articles and procedures, devise methods to detain prisoners;
translations.idiomatic: At first they multiplied charges and procedures to detain prisoners;

sentences.zh: 終則誅剝貨財，市恩出拔。

translations.literal: in the end they extort goods and wealth, trading favor for release.
translations.idiomatic: in the end they extorted wealth and traded favors for release.

sentences.zh: 外憑公道，內循私情，無理者轉務遷延，有理者卻思退縮。

translations.literal: Outwardly relying on public justice, inwardly following private feeling—those without reason instead strive for delay, while those with reason think of withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they invoked public justice while inwardly they followed private feeling: the guilty prolonged their cases, while the innocent shrank from pressing their claims.

sentences.zh: 積成訛弊，漸失紀綱。

translations.literal: Abuses accumulated and became corrupt practice, and discipline was gradually lost.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses piled up, discipline eroded, and proper order was gradually lost.

sentences.zh: 自今後切委逐處官吏州牧縣宰等，深體余懷，各舉爾職。

translations.literal: From now on we earnestly entrust the officials, prefectural governors, and county magistrates everywhere to enter deeply into our intent and each perform his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every prefectural governor, county magistrate, and local official was urgently entrusted to grasp the emperor's intent and perform his proper duty.

sentences.zh: 凡闕推究，速與剸裁。

translations.literal: Whatever lacks investigation, promptly judge and decide.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever had not been investigated was to be tried and decided at once.

sentences.zh: 如敢茍縱依違，遂成枉濫，或經臺訴屈，或投匭申冤，勘問不虛，其元推官典並當責罰，其逐處觀察使、刺史，別議朝典。

translations.literal: If anyone dares to indulge laxity and equivocation, thereby causing wrongful abuse, or if complaint reaches the Censorate or petition is placed in the grievance box, and investigation proves true, the original investigating officials and clerks shall all be punished; the regional inspectors and prefects in each place shall be separately dealt with under court statutes.
translations.idiomatic: If officials indulged delay or equivocation and caused injustice, or if complaints to the Censorate or the grievance box proved true on investigation, the original investigators were to be punished and the regional inspectors and prefects dealt with under court law.

sentences.zh: 宜令諸道州府，各依此處分，所管屬郡，委本道嚴切指揮。

translations.literal: All circuit prefectures and districts should be ordered to handle matters according to this disposition; the subordinate commanderies under their jurisdiction are entrusted to their circuits for strict direction.
translations.idiomatic: All circuit prefectures were to act accordingly, and each circuit was to give strict orders to the counties under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 」八月丁卯，敕：「三京、諸道州府刑獄，近日訪聞，依前禁系人，多不旋決，諸道宜令所在各委長吏，專切推窮，不得有滯淹。」

translations.literal: " On the day dingmao of the eighth month, an edict ordered: "In the prisons of the three capitals and the prefectures and districts of all circuits, we have recently learned upon inquiry that, as before, detained persons are mostly not promptly decided; all circuits should order the local chief officials to investigate with dedicated urgency, without delay."
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day in the eighth month, an edict reported that prisons in the three capitals and the circuits still held many detainees without prompt judgment, and ordered local chief officials to investigate urgently without delay.

sentences.zh: 四月，前濮州錄事參軍崔琮上言：「諸道獄囚，恐不依法拷掠，或不勝苦致斃，翻以病聞，請置病囚院，兼加醫藥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, former Recorder of Pu Prefecture Cui Cong memorialized: "Prisoners in the circuits may fear that interrogation by torture is not according to law, or that unable to bear suffering they die, yet it is reported as illness; we request establishment of a ward for sick prisoners, together with provision of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, former Pu Prefecture recorder Cui Cong proposed that circuit prisoners might die under illegal torture and be reported as ill, and asked that sick-prisoner wards be established with medical care.

sentences.zh: 」中書覆云：「有罪當刑，仰天無恨；

translations.literal: " The Secretariat replied: "When guilty one should be punished, looking to Heaven without resentment;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat replied that the guilty should accept punishment without resentment toward Heaven;

sentences.zh: 無病致斃，沒地銜冤。

translations.literal: to die without illness is to go to the ground bearing wrongful grievance.
translations.idiomatic: but to die without illness was to go to the grave still bearing a wrongful grievance.

sentences.zh: 燃死灰而必在至仁，照覆盆而須資異鑒。

translations.literal: To rekindle dead ashes surely lies in supreme benevolence; to illuminate an overturned basin requires extraordinary discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Rekindling dead ashes required supreme benevolence; illuminating an overturned basin required extraordinary discernment.

sentences.zh: 《書》著『欽哉』之旨，『《禮》』標『侀也』之文，因彰善於泣辜，更推恩於扇暍。

translations.literal: The Documents records the intent of "Revere!"; the Rites marks the text "Punishment!"—thereby displaying goodness in weeping for the wrongfully punished, and further extending grace in fanning the overheated.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents enjoin reverence and the Rites mark punishment—showing goodness in weeping for the wrongfully punished and extending grace to those overcome by heat.

sentences.zh: 所請置病囚院，望依，仍委長吏，專切經心。

translations.literal: The request to establish sick-prisoner wards is hoped to be granted; chief officials are further entrusted to attend to it with dedicated care.
translations.idiomatic: The request for sick-prisoner wards was granted, with chief officials entrusted to oversee it carefully.

sentences.zh: 或有病囚，當時遣醫人診候，治療後，據所犯輕重決斷。

translations.literal: If there are sick prisoners, physicians shall at once be sent to examine them; after treatment, sentence shall be decided according to the severity of the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Sick prisoners were to receive immediate medical examination and, after treatment, be sentenced according to the gravity of their offenses.

sentences.zh: 如敢故違，致病囚負屈身亡，本處官吏，並加嚴斷。

translations.literal: If anyone dares deliberately to violate this, causing a sick prisoner to die bearing wrongful grievance, the local officials shall all receive severe sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who deliberately violated this and caused a sick prisoner to die wrongfully were to be severely punished.

sentences.zh: 兼每及夏至，五日一度，差人洗刷枷匣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever the summer solstice arrives, once every five days persons shall be assigned to wash the cangues and fetters."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from the summer solstice onward, cangues and fetters were to be washed once every five days."

sentences.zh: 應順元年二月戊午，詔：「應三京、諸道州府系囚，據罪輕重，疾速斷遣。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu of the second month of the first year of Yingshun, an imperial pronouncement ordered: "All prisoners detained in the three capitals and the prefectures and districts of all circuits, according to the severity of crime, shall be swiftly sentenced and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day in the second month of Yingshun 1, an edict ordered that all prisoners in the three capitals and the circuits were to be sentenced and dispatched quickly according to the severity of their crimes.

sentences.zh: 比來停滯，須奏取裁，不便區分，故為留滯。

translations.literal: Recently cases have stagnated because memorials must be submitted for imperial decision, making timely distinction inconvenient and causing delay.
translations.idiomatic: Cases had stagnated because everything had to await imperial decision by memorial, which made timely judgment impossible.

sentences.zh: 今後凡有刑獄，據理斷遣。

translations.literal: Hereafter, whenever there are criminal cases, sentence and dispatch according to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all criminal cases were to be decided and dispatched on their merits.

sentences.zh: 如有敕推按，理合奏聞，不在此限。」

translations.literal: If there is an edict ordering investigation, it is proper to report in memorial; that is not within this limit."
translations.idiomatic: Cases ordered investigated by special edict still required memorial reporting and were excepted from this rule."

sentences.zh: 清泰元年五月丁丑，詔：「在京諸獄及天下州府見系罪人，正當暑毒之時，未免拘囚之苦，誠知負罪，特軫予懷。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou of the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai, an imperial pronouncement stated: "Prisoners now detained in the prisons of the capital and in the prefectures and districts throughout the realm, at the very time of oppressive summer heat, cannot avoid the suffering of confinement; knowing they bear guilt, we especially extend compassion in our breast.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the fifth month of Qingtai 1, an edict declared that prisoners in the capital and throughout the realm, confined in the heat of summer, could not escape their suffering even though guilty, and the emperor's heart went out to them.

sentences.zh: 恐法吏生情，滯於決斷。

translations.literal: We fear that judicial officers may indulge private feeling and delay in deciding.
translations.idiomatic: He feared that judicial officers might indulge themselves and delay judgment.

sentences.zh: 詔至，所在長吏親自慮問，據輕重疾速斷遣，無淹滯。」

translations.literal: When the pronouncement arrives, the local chief officials shall personally examine and question, and according to severity swiftly sentence and dispatch, without delay."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived, local chief officials were to examine prisoners personally and sentence them quickly according to severity, without delay."

sentences.zh: 晉天福二年八月，敕下刑部大理寺御史臺及三京、諸道州府：「今後或有系囚染疾者，並令逐處軍醫看候，於公廨錢內量支藥價，或事輕者，仍許家人看候。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Tianfu of Jin, an edict was issued to the Ministry of Punishments, the Court of Judicial Review, the Censorate, the three capitals, and the prefectures and districts of all circuits: "Hereafter, if any detained prisoner falls ill, military physicians everywhere shall be ordered to attend; medicine costs shall be allotted from public-office funds; or if the matter is light, family members may still be permitted to attend.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jin Tianfu 2, an edict to the Ministry of Punishments, Court of Judicial Review, Censorate, three capitals, and all circuits ordered that sick prisoners be treated by military physicians at public expense, and in light cases family attendance was permitted.

sentences.zh: 」四年九月，相州節度使桑維翰奏：「管內所獲賊人，從來籍沒財產，雲是鄴都舊例，格律未見明文。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month of the fourth year, Military Governor of Xiang Prefecture Sang Weihan memorialized: "Thieves captured within our jurisdiction have always had their property confiscated, said to be the old practice of the Yedu capital, but no explicit text is found in statutes and precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 4, Xiangzhou Military Governor Sang Weihan reported that thieves captured in his jurisdiction had always had their property confiscated as an old Yedu practice, though no statute explicitly authorized it.

sentences.zh: 」敕：「今後凡有賊人，準格定罪，不得沒納家資。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered: "Hereafter, for all thieves, sentence according to precedents; household property must not be confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that henceforth thieves were to be sentenced only under the precedents and their household property was not to be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 天下諸州，準此處分。

translations.literal: All prefectures throughout the realm shall follow this disposition.
translations.idiomatic: All prefectures throughout the realm were to follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 」三月庚午，詳定院奏：「前守洪洞縣主簿盧燦進策云：『伏以刑獄至重，朝廷所難，尚書省分職六司，天下謂之會府，且諸道決獄，若關人命，即刑部不合不知。

translations.literal: " On the day gengwu of the third month, the Court of Detailed Deliberation memorialized: "Former Acting Magistrate of Hongtong County Lu Can submitted a policy proposal stating: 'We humbly consider that criminal imprisonment is supremely grave and difficult for the court; the Department of State Affairs divides duties among six bureaus and is called the metropolitan office by the realm; moreover, when circuits decide cases involving human life, the Ministry of Punishments ought not to be uninformed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day in the third month, the Court of Detailed Deliberation reported that former Hongtong County magistrate Lu Can had proposed that because criminal cases were grave and the Ministry of Punishments should know when circuits decided capital cases.

sentences.zh: 欲請州府凡斷大辟罪人訖，逐季具有無申報刑部，仍俱錄案款事節，並本判官、馬步都虞候、司法參軍、法直官、馬步司判官名銜申聞，所貴或有案內情曲不圓，刑部可行覆勘。

translations.literal: We wish to request that whenever prefectures and districts finish sentencing capital offenders, each quarter they report whether or not they have notified the Ministry of Punishments, and also record the facts and circumstances of the case, together with the names and titles of the original judging official, commander of cavalry and infantry, judicial aide, legal examiner, and cavalry and infantry commission judges, so that if the circumstances within a case are incomplete, the Ministry of Punishments may conduct a rehearing.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that after each capital sentence prefectures report quarterly to the Ministry of Punishments with the case record and the names of all judging officials, so the ministry could rehear cases where the facts were incomplete.

sentences.zh: 如此則天下遵守法律，不敢輕易刑書，非惟免有銜冤，抑亦勸其立政者。

translations.literal: Thus the realm would observe the law and not lightly apply the penal code—not only avoiding wrongful grievance, but also encouraging those who establish administration.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the realm would observe the law, wrongful convictions would be avoided, and good administration would be encouraged.

sentences.zh: 』臣等參詳，伏以人命至重，國法須精，雖載舊章，更宜條理，誠為允當，望賜施行。

translations.literal: ' Your subjects have examined this in detail; we humbly consider that human life is supremely grave and state law must be precise; although recorded in old regulations, it should further be set in order; it is truly appropriate and we hope it may be granted implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The reviewers found human life supremely grave and state law requiring precision; though old regulations existed, further ordering was appropriate, and they asked that the proposal be implemented.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔曰：「刑獄之難，古今所重，但關人命，實動天心，或有冤魂，則傷和氣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an imperial pronouncement stated: "The difficulty of criminal imprisonment is valued in past and present alike; whenever human life is involved, it truly moves the mind of Heaven; if there are wrongful souls, harmonious qi is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, an edict declared that criminal cases had always been grave because they touched human life, moved Heaven's mind, and harmed harmonious order when injustice occurred.

sentences.zh: 應諸道州府，凡有囚徒，據推勘到案款，一一盡理，子細檢律令格敕。

translations.literal: All circuit prefectures and districts, whenever there are prisoners, according to the case facts reached by investigation, shall examine each fully in reason and carefully check statutes, orders, and precedents.
translations.idiomatic: All circuit prefectures were to examine every prisoner thoroughly on the facts investigated and check carefully against statutes, orders, and precedents.

sentences.zh: 其間或有疑者，準令文讞，大理寺亦疑，申尚書省，省寺明有指歸，州府然後決遣。」

translations.literal: If among them there are doubtful points, follow the statutory text for judgment; if the Court of Judicial Review also doubts, report to the Department of State Affairs; when the department and court have clear direction, the prefectures and districts may then sentence and dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: Where doubt remained, judgment was to follow the statutes; if the Court of Judicial Review still doubted, the case went to the Department of State Affairs, and only after clear direction from the department and court could prefectures sentence and dispatch."

sentences.zh: 五年三月丙子，詔曰：「自大中六年已來，嫠耳稱冤，決杖流配，訴雖有理，不在申明。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi of the third month of the fifth year, an imperial pronouncement stated: "Since the sixth year of Dazhong, widows who pierce the ear to proclaim grievance have been beaten with the staff and banished; although the complaint may be justified, it is not among matters that may be reported.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the third month of year 5, an edict noted that since Dazhong 6 widows who pierced the ear to proclaim grievance had been beaten and banished even when their complaints were justified, and such cases were no longer reportable.

sentences.zh: 今後據其所陳，與為勘斷，剺耳之罪，準律別科。

translations.literal: Hereafter, according to what they state, investigate and decide for them; the crime of piercing the ear shall be sentenced separately according to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth their statements were to be investigated and decided on their merits, and the crime of ear-piercing was to be punished separately under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 」六年秋七月庚辰，詔曰：「政教所切，獄訟惟先，推窮須察於事情，斷遣必遵於條法，用宏欽恤，以致和平。

translations.literal: " On the day gengchen of the seventh month of autumn in the sixth year, an imperial pronouncement stated: "What government and instruction urgently require is that litigation come first; investigation must observe the facts of the matter; sentencing and dispatch must follow the articles of law—thereby extending reverent compassion to achieve peace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day in the seventh month of year 6, an edict declared that litigation came first in government, investigation must observe the facts, and sentencing must follow the law to extend compassionate rule and achieve peace.

sentences.zh: 應三京、鄴都及諸道州府，見禁諸色人等，宜令逐處長吏，常切提撕，疾速決遣，每務公當，勿使滯淹。

translations.literal: In the three capitals, the Yedu capital, and the prefectures and districts of all circuits, all persons now detained of every kind should be ordered by the local chief officials constantly to be urged and supervised, swiftly sentenced and dispatched, always striving for fairness, without allowing delay.
translations.idiomatic: In the three capitals, Yedu, and all circuit prefectures, chief officials were constantly to supervise all detainees, sentence them swiftly and fairly, and allow no delay.

sentences.zh: 」天福八年四月壬申，敕：「朕自臨寰宇，思致和平，思將以四海為家，慮有一物失所。

translations.literal: " On the day renshen of the fourth month of the eighth year of Tianfu, an edict ordered: "We, since assuming rule over the realm, think to achieve peace, think to make the four seas our household, and fear that even one being may lose its place.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day in the fourth month of Tianfu 8, an edict proclaimed that since assuming rule the emperor sought peace for all under heaven and feared that even one person might suffer wrongly.

sentences.zh: 每念狴牢之內，或多枉撓之人，屬此炎蒸，倍宜軫憫，冀絕滯淹之嘆，用資欽恤之仁。

translations.literal: Whenever we think of those within the prisons, many may be persons wrongfully oppressed; at this season of blazing heat, compassion is doubly fitting, hoping to end the lament of prolonged detention and thereby supply the benevolence of reverent compassion.
translations.idiomatic: He thought often of those in prison who might be wrongfully oppressed, and in this season of heat compassion was doubly needed to end prolonged detention and embody merciful rule.

sentences.zh: 應三京、鄴都及諸道州府見禁罪人等，宜令逐處長吏，嚴切指揮本推司及委本所判官，疾速結絕斷遣，不得淹延，及致冤濫，仍付所司。」

translations.literal: All prisoners now detained in the three capitals, the Yedu capital, and the prefectures and districts of all circuits should be ordered by the local chief officials to direct strictly the investigating offices and entrust the local judging officials to conclude and sentence swiftly, without delay that leads to wrongful abuse; this is further entrusted to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: All prisoners in the three capitals, Yedu, and the circuits were to be concluded and sentenced swiftly by local chief officials through the investigating offices and judges, without delay or injustice; the responsible offices were charged with enforcement."

sentences.zh: 開運二年五月壬戌，殿中丞桑簡能上封事曰：「伏以天地育萬物，廣博厚之恩；

translations.literal: On the day renxu of the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyun, Palace Administration Director Sang Jianneng submitted a sealed memorial stating: "We humbly consider that Heaven and Earth nurture the ten thousand things with broad, generous, and deep favor;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the fifth month of Kaiyun 2, Palace Administration Director Sang Jianneng submitted a sealed memorial that Heaven and Earth nurture all things with broad and deep kindness;

sentences.zh: 帝王牧黎元，行寬大之令。

translations.literal: emperors and kings shepherd the black-haired people and enact lenient orders.
translations.idiomatic: and emperors shepherd the people with lenient decrees.

sentences.zh: 是知恤刑緩獄，乃為政之先；

translations.literal: thus we know that compassionate punishment and eased imprisonment are the first priorities of governance;
translations.idiomatic: Thus compassionate punishment and eased imprisonment come first in government;

sentences.zh: 布德行惠，實愛民之本。

translations.literal: to spread virtue and extend grace is truly the foundation of cherishing the people.
translations.idiomatic: and spreading virtue and grace is the foundation of loving the people.

sentences.zh: 今盛夏之月，農事方殷，是雷風長養之時，乃動植蕃蕪之際。

translations.literal: Now in the month of full summer, agricultural work is at its height; it is the season when thunder and wind nurture growth, the time when moving and rooted beings flourish abundantly.
translations.idiomatic: Now in high summer, when farming was at its height—the season of thunder and wind when all living things flourished—

sentences.zh: 宜順時令，以宏至仁。

translations.literal: One should follow the seasonal ordinance to extend supreme benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: the season called for following its ordinance and extending supreme benevolence.

sentences.zh: 竊以諸道州府都郡縣應見禁罪人，或有久在囹圄，稍滯區分，胥吏侮文，枝蔓乃眾。

translations.literal: We venture that among prisoners now detained in the prefectures, districts, commanderies, and counties of all circuits, some have long been in prison, their cases slightly delayed in judgment; clerks and runners despise the documents, and branching procedures multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Among prisoners held in circuit prefectures and counties, some had long languished in jail while clerks multiplied procedural branches and despised the written law.

sentences.zh: 捶楚之下。

translations.literal: Under beating and flogging,
translations.idiomatic: Under beating and flogging,

sentences.zh: 或陷無辜；

translations.literal: some are trapped though innocent;
translations.idiomatic: some were trapped though innocent;

sentences.zh: 縲紲之中，莫能自理。

translations.literal: within fetters and bonds, none can clear themselves.
translations.idiomatic: and within fetters none could clear themselves.

sentences.zh: 茍一人拘系，則數人營財，物用既殫，工業亦罷。

translations.literal: If one person is detained, then several persons raise funds; goods are exhausted and crafts cease.
translations.idiomatic: When one man was detained, several families spent their substance to ransom him, exhausting their goods and halting their work.

sentences.zh: 若此之類，實繁有徒，切恐官吏因循，浸成斯弊。

translations.literal: Cases of this kind are truly numerous; we urgently fear that officials follow routine and this abuse gradually becomes established.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases were numerous, and he feared that if officials followed routine this abuse would become entrenched.

sentences.zh: 伏乞降詔旨，令所在刑獄，委長吏親自錄問，量罪疾速斷遣，務絕冤濫，勿得淹留，庶免虛禁平人，妨奪農力，冀召和氣，以慶明時。

translations.literal: We humbly beg that an edict be issued ordering the prisons everywhere to entrust chief officials personally to record and question prisoners, measure crimes and swiftly sentence and dispatch, striving to end wrongful abuse, without detention, so that innocent commoners may not be falsely imprisoned, agricultural labor may not be hindered, and harmonious qi may be summoned to celebrate an enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that an edict order chief officials personally to question prisoners in every jail, sentence them swiftly according to their crimes, end injustice and delay, spare innocent commoners and farm labor, and summon harmonious order for an enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「囹圄之中，縲紲之苦，奸吏茍窮於枝蔓，平人用費於貨財，由茲滯淹，兼致屈塞。

translations.literal: " An edict stated: "Within prisons, the suffering of fetters—corrupt officials indulge in branching procedures, common people expend wealth on goods; thereby delay arises and wrongful obstruction as well.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that in prisons corrupt officials multiplied procedural branches while common people spent their wealth, causing delay and wrongful obstruction.

sentences.zh: 桑簡能體茲軫憫，專有敷陳，請長吏躬親，免獄官抑逼，深為允當，宜再頌行。

translations.literal: Sang Jianneng has entered into this compassionate concern and set it forth exclusively, requesting that chief officials attend in person and spare prisoners from pressure by jail officials; this is deeply appropriate and should again be proclaimed for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Jianneng had grasped this compassionate concern and proposed that chief officials attend in person and spare prisoners pressure from jail officials; the proposal was approved and ordered proclaimed again.

sentences.zh: 宜依。

translations.literal: Compliance is appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Compliance was ordered.

sentences.zh: 」十月甲子，秘書省著作郎邊玕上封事曰：「臣聞從諫如流，人君之令範；

translations.literal: " On the day jiazi of the tenth month, Compiler in the Secretariat Bian Gan submitted a sealed memorial stating: "Your subject has heard that to follow remonstrance like a flowing stream is the fine model of a ruler;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day in the tenth month, Secretariat compiler Bian Gan submitted a sealed memorial that to follow remonstrance like a flowing stream was the ruler's finest model;

sentences.zh: 極言無隱，臣子之常規。

translations.literal: to speak to the utmost without concealment is the constant rule of ministers and subjects.
translations.idiomatic: and to speak frankly without concealment was the constant duty of a subject.

sentences.zh: 蓋欲表大國之任人，致萬邦之無事，前文備載，可舉而行。

translations.literal: This is meant to display a great state's employment of men and bring the ten thousand states to peace; former texts record it fully and it may be raised and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: This was how a great state employed worthy men and brought the myriad regions to peace, as former texts fully recorded and might be enacted now.

sentences.zh: 伏以皇帝陛下，德合上玄，運膺下武，旰食宵衣而軫念，好生惡殺以推仁，幾措典刑，固無冤枉。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty's virtue accords with the Supreme Heaven and your mandate received the Martial Below; eating late and rising early in compassionate concern, cherishing life and hating killing to extend benevolence, you have nearly set aside canonical punishments and assuredly there is no wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue matched Heaven, he toiled from dawn to dusk in compassion, cherished life and hated killing, and had nearly set canonical punishments aside so that injustice scarcely occurred.

sentences.zh: 然以照臨之內，州郡尤多，若不再具舉明，伏恐漸成奸弊。

translations.literal: Yet within the realm illuminated by your grace, prefectures and districts are especially numerous; if this is not again set forth clearly, we humbly fear corrupt abuse will gradually arise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within the realm the prefectures were many, and unless the matter was set forth clearly again, corrupt abuses might gradually arise.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見諸道刑獄，前朝曾降敕文，凡是禁系罪人，五日一度錄問。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that in the prisons of the circuits, the former court once issued an edict that all detained prisoners should be recorded and questioned once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: He noted that a former edict had required all detained prisoners in the circuits to be questioned once every five days.

sentences.zh: 但以年月稍遠，漸致因循。

translations.literal: But as years and months have grown somewhat distant, routine has gradually set in.
translations.idiomatic: But as time passed, the rule had gradually fallen into neglect.

sentences.zh: 或長吏事煩，不暇躬親點檢；

translations.literal: sometimes chief officials are busy with affairs and have no leisure to inspect in person;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes chief officials were too busy to inspect in person;

sentences.zh: 或胥徒啟幸，妄要追領證明。

translations.literal: sometimes clerks and runners seek advantage and falsely demand pursuit and summoning of witnesses.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes clerks and runners sought advantage and falsely demanded witnesses be summoned.

sentences.zh: 慮有涉於淫刑，即恐傷於和氣。

translations.literal: Fearing involvement in excessive punishment, harmonious qi may thereby be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: He feared excessive punishment and harm to harmonious order.

sentences.zh: 伏乞特降詔敕。

translations.literal: We humbly beg that a special edict be issued.
translations.idiomatic: He humbly asked that a special edict be issued.

sentences.zh: 自今後諸道並委長吏五日一度，當面同共錄問，所冀處法者無恨，銜冤者獲伸。

translations.literal: From now on in all circuits entrust chief officials once every five days to record and question prisoners together face to face, so that those punished by law harbor no resentment and those bearing wrongful grievance obtain redress.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth chief officials in all circuits were to question prisoners together face to face every five days, so that the punished would harbor no resentment and the wronged would obtain redress.

sentences.zh: 俾令四海九州，鹹歌聖德；

translations.literal: thereby causing the four seas and nine provinces all to sing of sage virtue;
translations.idiomatic: So that all within the four seas and nine provinces might sing of sage virtue;

sentences.zh: 五風十雨，永致昌期。

translations.literal: the five winds and timely rains forever bringing a flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: and timely winds and rains forever bring a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「人之命無以復生，國之刑不可濫舉。

translations.literal: " An edict stated: "Human life, once lost, cannot live again; the state's punishments must not be applied indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that human life, once lost, could not be restored and state punishments must not be applied indiscriminately.

sentences.zh: 雖一成之典，務在公平；

translations.literal: Although the canon is fixed once for all, fairness must be pursued;
translations.idiomatic: Though the law was fixed, fairness had to be pursued;

sentences.zh: 而三覆其詞，所宜詳審。

translations.literal: and three rehearings of the case are what should be examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: and three rehearings of the case were what should be examined in detail.

sentences.zh: 凡居法吏，合究獄情。

translations.literal: All who hold office in law should thoroughly investigate prison circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: All judicial officers should thoroughly investigate prison circumstances.

sentences.zh: 邊玕近陟周行，俄陳讜議，更彰欽恤，宜允申明。」

translations.literal: Bian Gan has recently been promoted in the court ranks and soon offered forthright counsel, further displaying reverent compassion; approval and clarification are appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Gan, recently promoted at court, had soon offered forthright counsel displaying further reverent compassion; approval and clarification were ordered."

sentences.zh: 三年十一月丁未，左拾遺竇儼上疏曰：「臣伏睹名例律疏云：死刑者，古先哲王，則天垂象，本欲生之，義期止殺，絞斬之坐，皆刑之極也。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei of the eleventh month of the third year, Left Reminder Dou Yan submitted a memorial stating: "Your subject has observed that the commentary on the General Principles Statutes says: Capital punishment—ancient sage kings, conforming to Heaven's displayed signs, originally wished to give life; the meaning aims at stopping killing; the punishments of strangulation and decapitation are both the extreme of penalties.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the eleventh month of year 3, Left Reminder Dou Yan submitted a memorial citing the General Principles commentary that capital punishment, as the ancient sages understood it, aimed at preserving life and stopping killing, and that strangulation and decapitation were the extreme penalties.

sentences.zh: 又準天成三年閏八月二十三日敕，行極法日，宜不舉樂，減常膳；

translations.literal: Furthermore, according to the edict of the twenty-third day of the intercalary eighth month of the third year of Tiancheng, on the day the extreme penalty is carried out, music should not be performed and the regular meal should be reduced;
translations.idiomatic: According to a Tiancheng 3 edict, on days when the extreme penalty was carried out music was not to be performed and the regular meal was to be reduced;

sentences.zh: 又刑部式，決重杖一頓處死，以代極法，斯皆人君哀矜不舍之道也。

translations.literal: furthermore, in the formats of the Ministry of Punishments, death by one heavy beating with the staff in place of the extreme penalty—all these are the way of the ruler's compassionate pity that cannot bear to let go.
translations.idiomatic: and under Ministry of Punishments formats, death by one heavy beating with the staff might substitute for the extreme penalty—all expressions of the ruler's compassionate pity.

sentences.zh: 竊以蚩尤為五虐之科，尚行鞭樸；

translations.literal: We venture that even Chiyou, who established the five cruel punishments, still applied flogging;
translations.idiomatic: Even Chiyou, who established the five cruel punishments, still applied flogging;

sentences.zh: 漢祖約三章之法，止有死刑。

translations.literal: the Han founder's three-article law had only the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: and the Han founder's three-article law recognized only the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 絞者筋骨相連，斬者頭頸異處，大辟之目，不出兩端，淫刑所興，近聞數等。

translations.literal: Strangulation leaves sinew and bone connected; decapitation separates head and neck; the categories of great execution do not go beyond these two ends; excessive punishments that have arisen recently are heard to number several kinds.
translations.idiomatic: Strangulation left body intact while decapitation severed head from neck; great execution had only these two forms, yet recently several kinds of excessive punishment had been heard of.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣外地，不守通規，肆率情性，或以長釘貫篸人手足，或以短刀臠割人肌膚，乃至累朝半生半死，俾冤聲而上達，致和氣以有傷。

translations.literal: This is because in outer regions they do not observe the general regulations but indulge their dispositions at will—sometimes driving long nails through people's hands and feet, sometimes using short knives to slice people's flesh, even leaving persons half alive and half dead for successive courts, causing cries of grievance to reach above and harming harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: This was because remote regions ignored the general regulations and indulged their whims—driving long nails through hands and feet, slicing flesh with short knives, leaving victims half alive for days—so cries of grievance reached the throne and harmed harmonious order.

sentences.zh: 將宏守位之仁，在峻惟行之令，欲乞特下明敕，嚴加禁斷者。

translations.literal: To extend the benevolence of keeping one's place and to enforce sternly the command of acting with deliberation, we wish to beg that a clear edict be specially issued to forbid and cut off such practices.
translations.idiomatic: To extend the benevolence proper to the throne and enforce stern execution of the law, he asked that a clear edict strictly forbid such practices.

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「文物方興，刑罰須當，有罪宜從於正法，去邪漸契於古風。

translations.literal: " An edict stated: "As culture and institutions are rising, punishments must be appropriate; the guilty should follow the proper law, and removing evil should gradually accord with ancient custom.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied that as culture was rising, punishments must be appropriate, the guilty should follow proper law, and removing evil should accord with ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 竇儼所貢奏章，實裨理道，宜依所奏，準律令施行。」

translations.literal: The memorial Dou Yan presented truly assists the way of good order; compliance with his memorial is appropriate, to be carried out according to statutes and orders."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yan's memorial truly assisted good order; compliance was ordered and it was to be carried out according to statutes and orders."

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年正月，敕：「政貴寬易，刑尚哀矜，慮滋蔓之生奸，實軫傷而是念。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Qianyou of Han, an edict ordered: "Government values leniency and ease; punishment esteems compassionate pity; we fear that spreading abuses breed wrongdoing, and truly extend compassionate concern in this thought.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Han Qianyou 2, an edict declared that government valued leniency and punishment compassionate pity, fearing that spreading abuses bred wrongdoing and extending heartfelt concern.

sentences.zh: 今屬三元改候，四序履端，將冀和平，無如獄訟。
